GEMSDOE.title: GEMSDOE — Geologic Mapping Prize Challenge
GEMSDOE.description: Evidence-backed site for the DOE GEMS Prize Challenge on DrivenData ($300,000 total prize — $50k initial, $250k final — ending 2026-12-03): predicting geothermal faults in the GeoDAWN region under a distance-weighted Tversky metric, with a 19-band feature stack. Session-19 status read from STATUS.md: all four block-holdout folds are now committed and the memorisation-vs-transfer gap is reported as a spread rather than a point — fold 0 +0.0114, fold 1 −0.0070, fold 2 +0.0139, fold 3 +0.0093, mean +0.006904, spread 0.020935, positive in 3 of 4 — and because no fold reaches the ≥12 resampling units a readable block-bootstrap interval needs, the scorer itself flags every per-fold interval `interval_readable: false`, so the honest reading is 'no clear memorisation, no clear transfer gain' with the full-grid 0.099859 (reproduced digit-for-digit on a runner) retained as the selection statistic. The pseudo-label contrast is measured on every committed truth population and points in opposite directions on the two components, but it has now FIRED TWICE and STATUS.md is explicit that 'quoting either one alone would overstate the precision'. The first fire gave held-out blocks 0.0806 → 0.1841 (+0.1036, P=0.999) on the new-fault-like proxy against 0.2113 → 0.1239 (−0.0874, P=0.001) on catalogue labels, deriving TRADE_OFF_PROXY_GAINS_CATALOGUE_LOSSES; the second fire — same seed, same config, same partition, different runner — measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue −0.1079, deriving GAIN_ON_THE_COMBINED_SURROGATE. That is a ~0.036 run-to-run swing on the proxy arm, the same order of magnitude as the +0.0313 union contrast itself, and the two scopes disagree in sign on the union (+0.0313 held-out against −0.0375 trained-on), which STATUS.md calls instability rather than a result. Read against the bar its own FIELD rule uses (paired block bootstrap P ≥ 0.95), the union contrast reaches P = 0.916 with an interval spanning zero on 8 scoreable blocks, so it is suggestive and not established; both fires' numbers remain in git history but the second overwrote the first's committed evidence files. Both verdicts carry `shippable_evidence: false`, and the circularity is derived rather than asserted, because the pseudo-label path is the same proxy_catalogue.tif the proxy truth is cut from. STATUS.md also defuses one coincidence on purpose: the baseline's union held-out DTI of 0.197183 resembles the public leaderboard's top score of 0.1972, and the two are unrelated quantities. A third population, the disjoint 122,652-pixel union (60,988 + 61,664, disjointness verified at score time), scores the shipped artifact 0.207431 CI95 [0.192924, 0.222879] and puts the adopted emission policy 2nd of 10 distinct emissions (50 swept, 40 pruned as duplicates) — the 1-pixel widening that beats it scores +0.0054 at P=0.815, below both pre-registered bars (P ≥ 0.95 and +0.010), so the adopted policy holds on a third population too, while the union arm that landed as run 35477119490 is recorded as suggestive, under-powered and not shippable. Session 18's pre-registered FIELD-selection rule (docs/FIELD_SELECTION_RULE.md), machine-gated first in reblend.yml, still returns KEEP mean12. Session 21 (2026-09-21) closed the standing data-placement blocker inside a sandbox: scripts/assemble_data_bridge.py reassembled all three official rasters from committed parts in 2.8 s, verifying every part sha256 and each whole-file sha256 against data/bridge/manifest.json (training_features.tif 418,912,844 B, labels.tif 425,830 B, sample_submission.tif 1,599,597 B), after which prepare_data.py PASSED on the placed bytes (3292x3730, 19 bands, EPSG:32611, 100 m, aligned bounds, band tags present). The CPU-only route to a submission was then re-executed end to end and reproduced the committed artifact byte for byte — the same selected policy (floor 0.000974, thin, width 0 px, union DTI 0.160259 on selection fold 0) and a submission.tif whose sha256 matches the committed baseline, with the generalisation audit re-scoring untouched fold 1 at catalogue 0.06597 / proxy 0.071107 / combined 0.078916, reproduced=True and max absolute delta 0.00016874; the two reports differ only in timings. validate_submission.py passed all 8 checks on the freshly written file, and the pre-registered support cap did its job visibly by excluding the highest-scoring candidate (floor 0.009487, union 0.197198) for emitting 487,813 px, 9.4% of the footprint, with the reason printed in the report. MLBRainDelay.title: MLB Rain Delay — Live Scoreboard with Weather & Delay Tracking
MLBRainDelay.description: Zero-dependency static MLB scoreboard that adds, for every game on a date's slate, the official weather picture at the ballpark and a verified record of every delay, postponement and suspension. Three pages (index.html scoreboard, delays.html all-games delay feed, game.html single game) read the MLB StatsAPI for status, gameInfo.delayDurationMinutes, play-by-play game_advisory events and box-score info labels, and the US National Weather Service (points -> hourly forecast -> active alerts) for weather, falling back to Environment and Climate Change Canada for Rogers Centre and to Open-Meteo elsewhere (always flagged non-government-source). Delay rows are produced only from official MLB status data, never from a forecast; the derived forecast-risk chip prints its own six thresholds (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/NONE/COVERED/UNKNOWN) verbatim from RISK_RULES in assets/js/weather.js. A captured copy of the full GET /api/v1/gameStatus registry holds 210 status rows, and three offline Node test suites assert 56 checks in total (26 delays, 24 weather, 6 render).

By design it does not scan Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit or news sites — the repository states a keyless static page has no verifiable way to read them — and instead links official club news, @MLB_PR, NWS and SPC pages under a Manual review heading. Its own Limitations section also records that browser CORS for the Environment Canada endpoint is still unverified and that some special-event venues have no coordinates.

irregularities.title: The overlay stamped only a timestamp, so a repo that moved after its prose was read was undetectable — fixed with a recorded commit SHA, which then caught five moves in one pass
irregularities.detail: Design defect found and fixed during this audit. README task #3 asked for a per-entry `lastVerified` date so a reader could tell which descriptions were re-read this cycle. That was implemented, and IRR-47 immediately proved it inadequate: ShoulderPain's default branch moved at 2026-09-20T02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after its stamp of 02:41:19Z was written, so the stamp said 're-read in the latest pass' about a repository state that no longer existed. A date answers 'when did someone look', not 'is what they wrote still what is there'. Every entry therefore now also carries `verifiedAtSha` — the 7-character default-branch commit its prose was read against — and tools/build_data.py compares it with the live `lastCommitSha` at build time, emitting `proseStale` per entry and `counts.proseStale` in aggregate. The comparison is exact and free: no re-reading required, and a future session can list every entry whose prose is provably behind its repository before deciding what to read. Entries whose prose was carried forward record the prior audit's SHA rather than being left blank, so a carried entry is stale only if its repository actually moved. MasterSite's own entry is the one deliberate exception: its description describes this directory rather than a fetched README, so it is stamped with the SHA current when the description was last written and will always read stale immediately after a push. Limitation that remains: a matching SHA proves the prose was read against those bytes, not that it is still *true* — a repository can be accurate at one commit and wrong at the next without either changing (IRR-04 to IRR-06). What each build actually reported, in order: the first build after `verifiedAtSha` was added flagged 3 entries behind their repositories — GEMSDOE (session 19 had landed, superseding the session-18 status the description quoted), SFWeather (session 14) and ShoulderPain (a fourth commit) — all three of which had been re-read and stamped earlier in the *same* session, so a timestamp stamp would have called them current. After those were re-read, the next build flagged exactly 1: DrugAnalysis, whose prose had been *carried* from the prior audit at 6cb77f6 and whose v21.1 pre-1980 spine landed mid-build at b6cdb8a. Re-reading it, the next build flagged 2 more — SFWeather again (36fa2e4 to 42f9892, an automated data-only refresh that left README.md untouched, so its prose was re-verified by line-by-line diff and re-stamped rather than rewritten) and VacationSchedule (83663f7 to 6488222, which changed every window it recommends; IRR-52). The build after that flagged a fifth, OLBG-Competition (a371b63 to fee61ea), which had added an entire ice hockey pipeline and moved its test count 126 to 144 (IRR-54). Across the second pass the gate fired seven times on six distinct repositories, every one caught mechanically. Note which entries the detector caught: GEMSDOE, SFWeather and ShoulderPain had been re-read minutes earlier in the same session, but DrugAnalysis and OLBG-Competition were *carried* forward from earlier passes — precisely the entries a human auditor would least think to re-check, and the ones whose prose had actually gone false. The rebuild that reports `0 provably behind their repo` is the pass's completion gate: it means all 44 descriptions were read at the commit the repository is still at, which no timestamp can assert. Reproduce: run `python3 tools/build_data.py` and read the `PROSE-STALE` lines; the check is `entry.verifiedAtSha == repo head SHA`, using the same `gitHead` value the live dataset already records for every entry.

irregularities.title: GitHub Pages `status` is a live state machine, so a snapshot can record a healthy site as 'building' — the generator now waits and re-reads
irregularities.detail: Observed directly during this audit. The build that ran at 2026-09-20T02:57Z recorded `pagesBuilt: 43` of 44, the one exception being SFWeather with `pagesStatus: 'building'`. A re-read of GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/{repo}/pages for all 44 entries 12 seconds later returned `built` for every one, including SFWeather. The cause is not a defect in the repository or the directory: SFWeather's own automated nightly commit 42f9892 'data: refresh NOAA/NWS/NCEI/CPC sources [skip ci]' had landed at 02:57:39Z, seconds before the read, and GitHub Pages was mid-deploy. `status` is therefore a transient property of the deployment at the instant of the read, not a durable property of the repository — the same class of asynchrony as `size` (IRR-04 to IRR-06), but with a worse failure mode, because publishing '43 of 44 built' reads as 'one site is broken' when the truth is 'one site was rebuilding'. Fix applied to tools/build_data.py: when a Pages read returns any status other than 'built', the generator now re-reads that endpoint up to four times at six-second intervals before recording it, prints how many re-reads it needed, and still records a genuinely non-built status as-is with a warning if it persists — so a real broken build is never masked, only a transient one. Any future audit whose dataset reports fewer built sites than listed entries should re-read the endpoint before treating it as a finding.

irregularities.title: GitHub credentials expired mid-audit at ~2026-09-20T03:07Z, blocking the live re-verification, the push and the pull request for about two hours (resolved 04:54Z)
irregularities.detail: Recorded because it bounds what this audit can claim, and because the failure is silent in a dangerous way. The dataset published here was generated successfully at 2026-09-20T03:06:19Z (44 entries, 2,360 commits, all 44 Pages builds reporting `built`, 0 entries behind their repository head). Roughly one minute later every GitHub read began failing: `gh auth status` reports 'The github.com token in GH_TOKEN is no longer valid', `gh api repos/buffedlizard55-lab/MasterSite` returns HTTP 401 'Bad credentials', and — the part that makes this easy to miss — a plain unauthenticated `curl https://api.github.com/users/buffedlizard55-lab` also returns 401 rather than the usual 200, so the sandbox's egress credential itself is what expired, not a per-request token. Three consequences, stated plainly rather than papered over. (1) tools/verify_live.py was run after the expiry and returned 51 checks with every one a 'MISMATCH ... committed=200 live=401'; that output is an artifact of the auth failure and NOT a finding about the data, so tools/last_live_verify.json was restored from git to the last valid run (2026-09-20T01:17:26Z, 582 checks, 0 hard mismatches). A future session must not read the 401 run as 44 broken entries. (2) tools/audit_descriptions.py could not be re-run at all because it fetches each repository's README to diff against the published description; tools/last_description_audit.json is therefore a labelled PARTIAL artifact whose `unresolved` list predates the final edits to ShoulderPain and Elections. (3) `git push` failed with 'could not read Username for https://github.com', so at that moment the branch existed only as a local commit on arena/01a0bc90-mastersite, with no pull request opened and nothing merged. Two mitigations were verified while access still worked, so the published content itself is sound: the generator's own prose-staleness gate reported `0 provably behind their repo` for all 44 entries at the 03:06:19Z build, and no published artifact reads either verifier output file (tools/build_data.py, tools/build_verification.py, index.html and app.js were each grepped). Reproduce the failure: `gh auth status`, then `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.github.com/users/buffedlizard55-lab`. Resolution needs the account owner to reconnect GitHub; on reconnect the required sequence is re-run verify_live.py, re-run audit_descriptions.py, then push and open the pull request. Because these repositories commit continuously (IRR-42, IRR-50, IRR-52, IRR-54), the reconnect must also re-run build_data.py first — the 03:06:19Z snapshot will very likely already be behind by then. RESOLVED 2026-09-20: the owner reconnected GitHub at approximately 04:54Z. The prescribed sequence was then followed exactly rather than pushing the stale snapshot — a full build_data.py rebuild first, which reported 4 entries behind and grew total commits from 2,360 to 2,398, then re-read and rewrite, then rebuild again, repeating until the gate reported 0 provably behind (four builds, ten further moves, IRR-61), then build_verification.py, then all three verifiers, all of which ran clean: verify_live.py 582 of 582 checks with 0 hard mismatches and 0 drift, audit_descriptions.py 0 entries needing manual confirmation against 7 documented exceptions, and audit_kind.py 44 of 44 re-derived with 0 disagreements. The bogus 401 run and the PARTIAL description-audit artifact were both replaced by real runs. Final snapshot 2026-09-20T05:15:50Z, 2,413 commits, 62 irregularities.

irregularities.title: This directory's own GEMSDOE description quoted one replicate of a twice-fired measurement, which its source explicitly forbids — caught only because an evidence-only commit was read instead of waved through
irregularities.detail: A defect in this directory's prose, not in the repository's, and the most instructive catch of the audit because the mechanism that found it was not the one designed to. The prose-staleness gate reported GEMSDOE behind at 3093c6b; the intervening commit 0ca1466 is 'evidence(pseudo-labels): fold 0 with SGMC pseudo, paired vs no-pseudo baseline [skip ci]', touching 6 files at +1/-1 each and changing neither README.md nor STATUS.md. By the shortcut reasoning recorded for SFWeather in IRR-61 — automated commit, prose files untouched, therefore re-stamp — this would have been waved through. Instead the six files were fetched, because they are evidence rather than data refreshes, and data/evidence/pseudo_labels/fold0_two_population_contrast.json now reports verdict GAIN_ON_THE_COMBINED_SURROGATE with proxy +0.067719 and catalogue -0.107890. Those are not the +0.1036 (P=0.999) / -0.0874 (P=0.001) / TRADE_OFF_PROXY_GAINS_CATALOGUE_LOSSES values the published description quoted. Reading STATUS.md — byte-identical at both commits, so the gate could not have flagged it — explains why: the measurement has fired twice, and STATUS.md states that 'The effect is the size of the replicate noise. The first fire measured proxy +0.1036 (P = 0.999) and catalogue -0.0874 (P = 0.001); this fire, same seed, same config, same partition, different runner, measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue -0.1079', a ~0.036 run-to-run swing on the proxy arm of the same order as the +0.0313 union contrast itself. It adds that the two scopes disagree in sign on the union (+0.0313 held-out vs -0.0375 trained-on), which is 'instability, not a result', that read against the bar the repository's own FIELD rule uses (paired block bootstrap P >= 0.95) the union contrast reaches only P = 0.916 with an interval spanning zero on 8 scoreable blocks, making it 'suggestive, not established', and — the operative sentence — 'Eight blocks is not a sample. Both fires' numbers are in git history; the second overwrote the first's files, so quoting either one alone would overstate the precision.' The description did precisely that: it quoted the first fire alone and presented one derived verdict as the finding, so it was accurate about a number and misleading about the measurement. Corrected to carry both fires, the replicate swing, the scope sign disagreement, the P = 0.916 reading and the 0.197183-vs-0.1972 coincidence STATUS.md defuses on purpose. Two lessons recorded for future sessions. First, `verifiedAtSha` matching proves the prose was read against those bytes, not that it is true — the failing text had been read at 3093c6b minutes earlier and STATUS.md had not changed at all, so no SHA comparison could ever have flagged it; only reading the evidence the prose quotes did. Second, an evidence-only `[skip ci]` commit is not automatically benign: unlike a data refresh, evidence files are what a research description quotes, so they must be opened.
